visual_brief.subject: Five video-model offerings enter one enterprise selection surface with different trade-offs
verified_context: Microsoft and fal are rolling Kling v3 Pro, LTX-2.5 Fast and Pro, and MiniMax H3 Max and Max Turbo into Microsoft Foundry public preview.
The first-party announcement documents text-to-video and image-to-video options, model-specific hosting and published per-second pricing.
Output quality and performance were not independently compared in this edition, and preview and regional constraints remain material.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: A shared routing lens exposes choices without implying one universal winner.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: Five equal visual ribbons pass through one dark routing lens and project into a single restrained film surface, with no ribbon visually crowned.

candidate_notes.A: Constitution-compliant, but one terracotta strip reads as a preferred winner rather than an equal portfolio option.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant. The routing metaphor is clear but the left-heavy composition loses balance in the article crop.
candidate_notes.C: Selected. Five equal ribbons pass through one lens into a shared projection surface without implying an unsupported ranking.

crop_review.article_desktop: All five ribbons, the central lens and the projection surface remain inside the wide hero.
crop_review.article_mobile: The centered crop retains the lens and representative portions of all five equal inputs and the output surface.
crop_review.thumbnail: The five-to-one routing silhouette remains legible at 320px without relying on film detail.

golden_reference_comparison: The chosen image uses the golden references' quiet dimensional geometry, warm paper field and restrained terracotta signal. Its optical flow is more dynamic than the Terra reference but avoids interface imitation and preserves archive consistency; Golden Reference Fit is 88.
